title: Boolean Representation
body:
There is no boolean type in hardware. A [[Boolean]] is stored as an ordinary integer and
read by convention: **zero is false, anything non-zero is true**. That asymmetry matters,
because it means there is one false value and $2^n - 1$ true ones, so testing for truth is
"is it zero?" and never "is it equal to 1".

Which is exactly what the [[Status Bits]] give you. `tst d0` sets Z if the value is zero,
and `beq` / `bne` branch on it. A boolean in assembly is a condition code, not a variable.

C does the same thing under the hood, which is why `if (ptr)` works and why the C99 `bool`
is a normalising convenience rather than a new machine type. See
[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]].

Not to be confused with [[Binary Operations]], which work per bit; boolean truth testing
works on the whole value. `%0000_0010 & %0000_0001` is false-ish (0) while both operands are
individually true.
